data.narrative: The student wrapped Postgres with pybreaker and 1s timeouts, then proved the open state with a 10x GET /ready drill: five ConnectionTimeout 503s at ~4.1s followed by five 4ms circuit_open_fallback 503s. Retries with jitter were implemented only for transient OS errors, not OperationalError, avoiding the CONTEXT 4x load trap. BREAK distinguished a never-heal ops symptom from a stuck half-open bug; FIX added half-open trial logs shown on a probe breaker (open -> half-open -> closed).

strengths: Measured open-state speedup from ~4.1s to 4ms instead of claiming it.
Refused retries on ConnectionTimeout using Module 05/CONTEXT load math.
Half-open recovery proven on a probe breaker without inventing a Postgres restart.
growth_areas: TCP ConnectionTimeout still ~4.1s despite connect_timeout=1; first five requests remain expensive.
Production breaker half-open against a recovered DB was not exercised (no local Postgres).
data.recommendation: Module 07 runbook for circuit_open_fallback should tell on-call to check Postgres and wait reset_timeout rather than looping GET /ready, which would keep paying trial connect cost.
